subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out the design for a qilin creature—a quadruped with a deer-like body, dragon head, antlers, a flame/cloud mane, scaled torso, hooves, and a cloud-tufted tail—planning to build it with the 3D construction toolkit's limb, curve, and paint utilities.

I'm working out the skeleton: a spine chain running from hips to chest, a neck chain curving up to a head and jaw joint, a four-segment tail extending backward, and front/rear leg chains with specific joint positions and bend directions to get natural limb poses.

I'm sweeping the body along the spine chain with tapering radii and rounded caps, then adding chest and rump spheres for volume. For coloring I'm leaning toward a countershaded qilin palette—cream-white belly with golden-ochre back scales, drawing on the traditional golden-yellow look rather than a teal anime style.

Now I'm layering jade-green mane flames with red accents and glowing gold antler tips, nesting the countershade paint over a scaled back texture. For the neck and head, I'm building them from a swept chain with tapering radii, then constructing the skull as spheres and frustum shapes for the snout and jaws, figuring out joint positions so the head sits naturally at the end of the neck.

Still building the head geometry...

Now I'm designing the antlers as branching catmull-rom sweeps rooted at the skull, with a main path curving up and back and secondary spike branches sprouting from points along it, finished with glowing jade spheres at the tips.

Then I'm shaping the ears as extruded leaf-like fin outlines angled out, back, and up from the skull, and sketching plans for a fluffy cloud-style mane running along the neck using textured cards.

Adding cloud puffs and flame-blade cards...

For hooves I'm splitting each foot into two small cylinder halves to get a cloven look, offset slightly apart with a gold-dark tint, positioned at the tip bone. Then I'm adding soft cream cloud puffs clustered near the ankles for that "walking on clouds" effect, careful to keep their lowest point just above the floor so they don't clip through it.

Now I'm working out leg kinematics so the hoof tops land right at the floor, setting the limb end target just above the ankle and checking that the shoulder and hip heights give enough reach with the segment lengths to allow natural bending. I'm also tapering the limb radii and adding gold fetlock bands, deciding to skip the clockwork detailing for now.

For the tail, I'm shaping it like a lion's tuft with a chain of four joints curving back and down from the hips, parented correctly so it swings naturally. Then I'm laying out the spine chain starting at the hips joint and extending back toward the rump to give the body a rounded rear profile.

Adjusting the body radius function so the chest reads taller than the hindquarters while keeping the belly wide enough to seat the legs properly. The hip joints sit inside the body around y=1.1, with hind limbs parented to hips and front limbs parented to the last spine joint so the whole skeleton connects cleanly.

Now I'm working out the neck and head chain: three spine joints feed into a short neck curve built from a few catmull points, tapering radius toward the head, with the head joint parented to the final neck point and oriented slightly downward.

I'm assigning roles to each chain (spine, neck, tail, leg, jaw) and starting the head's facial geometry -- a skull sphere scaled for a dragon-lion shape, angled brow ridges in red-gold, and a muzzle built from a frustum box extending forward.

Now I'm detailing the jaw: lower jaw joint positioned and aimed forward, with a frustum box shape, plus a nose bump with dark nostrils, upper lip fangs, a goatee-style chin beard, and teeth spikes along the upper jaw. I'm double-checking the head's forward/down orientation against the frustum box's width and height conventions to make sure everything aligns correctly.

For the eyes, I'm placing decals on the skull surface using azimuth-based positioning, guarding against null hits, and mirroring the left eye per the documented pattern. I'm also lining up textures -- an anime-style eye, gold and green flame patterns, and a cloud swirl emblem -- to apply across the model.

Now I'm thinking through a forehead gem between the eyes, cloud swirl decals on the shoulders using surface-around placement with mirrored sides, flame tufts at the ankles, and a fan of flame cards ringing the back of the head using a ring frame anchored to the head's local space.

Working out cheek tufts with a handful of cards per side anchored to head-local frames, falling back to the nearest joint when needed. For mane detail, I'll add cloud puffs using subdivided icosahedron spheres with flat shading for a faceted look.

Now I'm settling on a gold-and-jade palette — gold tones for the body scales with a darker bronze edge, cream for the belly, jade and teal as accent colors, red and ink for contrast, and a warm gold for the horn. I'm deciding against a blue-green qilin look in favor of a gold-based scale paint with a shoulder-flame decal, using a slightly coarser scale texture on the body and a finer one on the head.

I'm reusing the same base coat paint for consistency, countershading the head and snout with lighter cream tones. For glow effects, I'm applying a moderate glow strength to the jade antler tips and gem, while letting the flame cards glow in their own colors so things don't look too flat.

Now I'm sketching out a flame-shaped SVG blade with a gradient running from deep teal at the root to jade near the top.

Still writing SVG shapes...

Adding more sweep placements...

Adding gold fetlock rings rotated flat around each leg, then positioning the forehead gem near the top-front of the skull using local offset coordinates.

Sketching antler placement...

Placing whiskers using bezier curves that sweep down and back from the head, with jade-colored tapering radii along their length.

Now I'm adding a beard with hanging card shapes under the jaw, teeth spikes on the upper jaw using cream-colored small cones, and dark spherical nostrils positioned near the snout tip.

I'm working out the nose bump geometry and nostril placement on top of it, then shaping the upper jaw as a tapered frustum box with the head paint color, and starting on a brow ridge rod extending outward from the eye region.

Now I'm positioning the eye decal and brow rod coordinates by estimating skull width and surface curvature, then moving on to body details like a cream belly stripe, shoulder swirl decals, and a line of tiny spikes running along the spine.

I'm deciding to skip the saddle-cloth, necklace, pendant, and jade collar loop as too risky or low-value given effort constraints, keeping the part count modest but reasonable. I'm adding haunch bulge spheres at the hips and similar shoulder bulges at the chest bone, along with a painted sphere for body texture.

For the swirl pattern, I'm designing a cloud-spiral decal using an SVG spiral path in red-gold tones with a darker outline stroke underneath, then applying it onto the body surface as a decal at the designated hit point.

Now I'm working out the hind limb geometry — setting root and foot positions, estimating segment lengths against the total distance, and alternating bend directions for each leg.

Naming each joint chain by limb and side (L/R prefixes), then setting up the spine chain parented to the hips using a catmull curve through the joint points.

For the body sweep I'm using an ellipse radius function that varies along the spine, tapering slightly wider at the rear, then adding haunch spheres on each side for the thigh bulges, checking that the leg x-offsets stay inside the haunch width so the silhouette reads correctly.

Now I'm building the tail as a sweep chain with a tapering radius and a tuft at the tip, shaping the skull as a scaled sphere positioned forward of the head bone, and setting up the neck as another tapered sweep connecting to the end of the spine chain.

I'm adding puff-like clusters of small icosahedra embedded along the neck to suggest mane texture, distributing them at a few points along the neck's length.

Now I'm applying a glow effect to jade-colored card elements, then defining a helper for constructing antler geometry by generating spline points off the head and sweeping a thin tube along that curve.

Continuing, I'm adding tine branches at intervals along the antler using small bezier curves, capping the tips and tine ends with glowing spheres, then double-checking the palette count stays consistent.
